title: SYNTHESIS v1 GATE (frontier, thinker): schema v2 + CLI v2 + the INTERPRETIVE-CODE rule list, precise enough to implement without judgment calls
description: The single gate of this epic. Consume the operator's addendum (docs/serenissima-addendum-legal-theory.md, tier-1 DIRECTIVE authority - it prevails over prior assumptions by its own instruction line), the coordinator amendment memo (.harness/coordinator-decisions-addendum.md, A1-A8, BINDING), the two research remainders (10-*.md, 11-*.md), and the v0 requirement baseline (synthesis-design-requirements.md SDR-01..SDR-30 and synthesis-refinements.md S-01..S-15 / R-1..R-16). Produce the single document the whole build consumes: docs/precedent-research/synthesis-v1-requirements.md. It must fix three things exactly: the schema v2 field list, the CLI v2 surface with migration semantics for existing schema_version 1 records, and the INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md v1 rule list. Low-verifiability judgment work: frontier tier per P-030 (ORCHESTRATION.md:136-160). Thinker role - no source edits, no code, no registry writes. Three build tasks (T-353, T-356, T-357) become claimable the moment this is verdicted, so vagueness here is the epic's single biggest failure mode: an implementer who has to make a judgment call is an implementer inventing constitutional material.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE: docs/precedent-research/synthesis-v1-requirements.md. Thinker role: no source edits, no writes under .harness/bin/, no PRECEDENT.md, no INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, no registry writes, no state.json.

INPUT LEDGER, opening section, mandatory: list the exact inputs consumed, and cite every requirement back to the one that produced it. Minimum: docs/serenissima-addendum-legal-theory.md BY SECTION (quote its own instruction line establishing that it is binding where marked DIRECTIVE and prevails over prior assumptions); .harness/coordinator-decisions-addendum.md by decision letter A1-A8; docs/precedent-research/10-horizontal-peer-precedent.md and 11-reasoning-burden-calibration.md by section; the v0 baseline SDR-NN / S-NN / R-NN items. A requirement with no cited input is explicitly labelled 'planner judgment, no research basis'.

STABLE NUMBERING: every requirement carries an id of the form V1-NN. The build tasks cite these ids in their DEVIATION notes and the verifiers replay against them, so an unnumbered requirement is unverifiable.

MANDATORY SECTION 'What this amends': for every v0 rule that schema v2 changes, name it, QUOTE the old rule, state the new rule, and classify the amending act under A4's taxonomy (determination / reinterpretation-declarative / reinterpretation-corrective-restrictive / reinterpretation-corrective-extensive / valuation). You MUST reach a verdict on at least these five, each either AMENDED (with the new text) or UNCHANGED (with the reason): SDR-01 (immutability of published fields, versus an in-place migration that adds fields to PR-001..PR-004); SDR-10 (citation token grammar, versus an external durable identifier such as a DOI); SDR-17.8 (tier symmetry governs overrules and voids but deliberately not supersedes); SDR-23 (cite is read-only and logs no event); R-2 in synthesis-refinements.md (repeated confirmation becomes a separate NON-BINDING reiterated flag on tier-4 records - the framing A2 partially overrules).

THE COMPLETE SCHEMA v2 FIELD TABLE, not a diff: reproduce the full field list in the v0 format (number | field | type | required? | class A/W/R | citation), covering every field including the unchanged ones. A partial table forces the implementer to join two documents and invent the merge. For each field state whether it is immutable after publication. Must fix at minimum: schema_version = 2; sources (MANDATORY - the interpretive resources actually consulted); validity_conditions as a field DISTINCT from scope_conditions, each with a one-sentence discriminating test precise enough that an implementer can classify a given string without judgment (validity_conditions = facts about the ENVIRONMENT the ratio presupposes: paths, tool versions, board mechanics, repo state; scope_conditions = the class of cases the ratio applies to); the typed operation field per A4 with its exact enum and sub-enums and a per-operation required-field matrix; interpretive_code_version.

SOURCES DISCIPLINE, stated mechanically: fix the exact rule the CLI enforces for A1 ('a corrective act that cites no sources is mechanically rejected') - which operation types it applies to, the exact exit code (reuse SDR-15's contract: 1 = REFUSAL, and say so rather than minting a new code), what a source token may be, and whether the refusal is event-logged. MUST extend SDR-10's token grammar with an EXTERNAL DURABLE IDENTIFIER kind (DOI at minimum), because docs/ is gitignored (verified: .gitignore:33) and a tracked registry record may never cite the addendum by local path - it would dangle for every reader who clones the repo. Fix the exact token form (e.g. doi:10.22201/iij.24487937e.2026.20.20316#3) and state whether such a token RESOLVES, WARNS or is UNCHECKED.

GRADED FORCE, computable from data that actually exists - this is the requirement most likely to be written unimplementably. Fix the force level enum and the exact computation from issuance tier plus recorded consistent applications. HARD CONSTRAINT the implementer cannot resolve for you: `cite` writes nothing, including events (SDR-23's own words) - there is no cite event in events.jsonl, so a formula that reads one is not implementable. Name the exact registry data the computation reads (the candidates that actually exist: cited_by back-references written as a publish-time side effect, relations[] of type follows/distinguishes on later records, confirmation flips, published_at) and demonstrate the formula is computable from it. DEFAULT, overrulable only with reasoning: force is COMPUTED ON READ, never a stored field - a stored force would have to mutate published records on every new citation, which SDR-01 forbids. If you make it stored, you MUST (a) amend SDR-01 explicitly in the 'What this amends' section and (b) instruct T-358 to publish that amendment as a record, and (c) note that T-355 then depends on T-354 and say so in plain words so the coordinator can serialize the dispatch.

DECAY WINDOW WITH A NAMED CLOCK: fix the unit, the threshold, and the exact observable the CLI reads. Wall-clock days are REJECTED as the unit unless you argue otherwise explicitly: this bench published an entire twenty-task epic and four records inside a single day (T-330..T-349, published_at 2026-08-10/11), so a wall-clock window measures burstiness, not neglect. Candidates: harness generations (state.json harness_generation), intervening published records, or a hybrid. Decay FLAGS a record as a reconsideration candidate and NEVER auto-expires it (addendum section 6, A2).

THE ANCHOR PROBLEM FOR A2'S OVERRULING - the one thing the build cannot invent. The thing A2 partially overrules (R-2 in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-refinements.md: 'Repeated confirmation becomes a separate, non-binding reiterated flag on tier-4 records') is NOT a PR record: it lives in a gitignored synthesis document, and the v0 relation grammar requires a target that is a PR-NNN and resolves to an existing record. FIX the resolution one of two ways, exactly: (a) extend the relation target grammar to accept a non-PR recorded-decision anchor (issuing task id plus document section, with the exact token form written out), or (b) require the T-344 framing to be published as a record FIRST and then overruled, naming who publishes it and with what tier. Whichever you choose, T-358 must be able to run the command without inventing anything, and T-353 must know exactly what to implement.

VALIDITY-CONDITIONS PASS: fix whether the staleness check extends `conflicts` (giving the new detector its number) or becomes a sibling verb (giving its exact name), its exit-code behavior (reuse SDR-15's 0/1/2/3/4 contract verbatim), and - mandatory - that it is READ-ONLY, mutates nothing, logs nothing, and flags RECONSIDERATION CANDIDATES rather than auto-expiring anything (A5, addendum section 6).

MIGRATION SEMANTICS FOR schema_version 1 RECORDS, exhaustively, because two build tasks are sequenced on the answer: (a) does the v2 CLI still LOAD a v1 record (dual-read) or refuse it (exit 4)? The answer is load-and-tolerate unless you argue otherwise, because T-353 ships the v2 CLI while the live registry is still v1 and the existing 100-test suite must stay green in that window; (b) exactly what the migration writes into each new mandatory field for the four seeds; (c) whether the in-place rewrite is a once-only exception to SDR-01, WHO authorizes it (A1 carries tier-1 authority via addendum section 3), and whether the exception itself must be published as a record; (d) that the migration is idempotent and guarded; (e) whether it is a CLI subcommand or a one-shot script, and where it lives.

CLI v2 SURFACE, exactly: every new and changed subcommand and flag with its exact long-form spelling, which are required, the exit-code contract (reuse SDR-15 verbatim; mint no new code without saying why), and the stdout contract for anything a verifier will grep. Environment constraint to respect and restate: stdlib only, must run under the bare python3 in this environment (3.9.6 - no match statement, no tomllib at module scope, no dataclass slots, no 3.10+ syntax), and reuse harness_common (guarded, atomic_write_json, log_event, now_iso) rather than reimplementing any of it.

THE TWO CARRIED DEFECTS FROM T-346 - decide, do not defer silently. (i) The test suite writes synthetic events into the live .harness/logs/events.jsonl with no test-root marker (T-346 measured roughly 598 such events). (ii) `supersedes` has no tier check: SDR-17.8 applies tier symmetry to overrules and voids only, and conflicts detector 3 excludes supersedes by a documented DECISION. For EACH: state whether it belongs in this epic, why, the exact fix, and its blast radius. HARD CONSTRAINT on (i): the fix must not change any harness_common function signature other CLIs depend on, and the whole substrate suite must still pass. HARD CONSTRAINT on (ii): adding a tier check to supersedes AMENDS a deliberate exclusion - say whether that amendment must be published as a record, and if so add it to the T-358 ledger.

THE INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md v1 RULE LIST, complete: every IC-NN rule T-356 will write, each with its id, its class (translation | preference | procedure) and its one-sentence normative content. Translation rules must at minimum fix the reading order A3 names (literal, then purposive, then systematic). Preference rules must fix how competing readings are ranked. Procedure rules must fix the ORDER OF APPLICATION and the code-version citation duty (every interpretive act cites the code version used - addendum section 4, A3). Also fix: the version string format, the exact location in the document where the version is declared so a CLI could read it, and the amendment route (constitutional-tier: overruling-grade protocol only, never an ordinary edit).

THE RECORD LEDGER FOR T-358: for each addendum section 2 through 7, state whether it gets its own tier-1 record and, if yes, give the record's subject slug, tier, tier_evidence anchor, operation type and the exact sources tokens it must carry. If a section gets no record, say which record subsumes it. Add the A2 partial-overruling record with its target anchor per the anchor decision above. T-358 must be able to publish this entire ledger without a single judgment call.

OUT OF SCOPE, stated flat so no downstream worker invents it: no NLAH mutation (claude.md / gemini.md are section 5A loop plus human gate, ORCHESTRATION.md:225-229); no state.json write, including the P-023 evolution.accepted_mutations backfill (tier-2 constitutional act, escalated at the join, never performed by a worker); no ORCHESTRATION.md edit; no full retrofit of the ~30 P-numbers; no hook and no hard gate (conflict detection stays an on-demand pass per D6); nothing from roadmap Parts III or IV.

SELF-CHECK BEFORE HANDOFF, stated in the handoff note: for requirements V1-NN covering graded force, the overruling anchor and the migration semantics, write out the exact command or code path an implementer would produce from your text. If you cannot, the requirement is not yet precise enough. This is the criterion the verifier will replay.

Hand off with `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py handoff --to-role verifier --agent <you>`. The note carries the schema v2 field table in compact form and the complete list of SDR/S/R items amended. Verification tier: doc/contract tier - internal consistency, citation coverage, and specifically whether the force formula, the overruling anchor and the migration semantics are implementable without judgment. The real adversarial test is T-359 replaying the built CLI against this document.

DECISION (hardest call 1): decay FLAGS and never silently lowers computed force; the drop to persuasive requires a recorded, tier-symmetric valuation/context-change act (V1-24/V1-30). Reason: A2 says decay flags for reconsideration; A4 says every metatextual weakening is a first-class recorded act, never silent; addendum s7 forbids silent divergence - a CLI silently demoting an uncited record would BE the silent weakening A4 forbids. Cost accepted: decay-to-persuasive is two steps, not one.

DECISION (hardest call 2): the A2 partial-overruling record (ledger row 5) is TIER 1 with operation determination, not tier 3 corrective. Tier: addendum s5 is not DIRECTIVE-tagged, but the prevail clause is unscoped to tags, A2 adopts it and directs formal publication, and the memo's scope paragraph groups it with the tier-1 records. Operation: 10 F6 - it is a forward-looking choice on new doctrine, not a claim that R-2 was erroneous ab initio. If the verifier reads s5 as pure research context, row 5 demotes to tier 3 and the ledger still runs (target tier 3, symmetry satisfied either way).
